introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2025. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub mark in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH paper are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

Calculators are Allowed.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees sans source consultable. Les faits cites (lieux, institutions, exemples) sont des faits reconnus ; aucune statistique precise n'est avancee. Contenu a faire relire par un geographe avant toute mise en avant.

Fautes d'impression du sujet conservees dans les enonces : « George » (gorge), « hallow » (hollow), « chanel » (channel), « Floodpalin » (floodplain), « under development », « TWO importance », « Briefly describe 1HREE ». Elles sont lues comme les termes usuels dans les corriges.

Question 4(b)(i) : le sujet ne dit pas si « meat processing » est un processus ou un produit ; il est classe en processus (c'est une operation) et le corrige precise qu'une reponse « produit » justifiee est creditee. Aucun bareme officiel.
Question 4(a)(i) : les indicateurs sont decrits sans valeur chiffree (aucune statistique precise n'est avancee).

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) (i) Describe **THREE** indicators of under development.
(ii) State **THREE** techniques of climate smart agriculture.

(6+3=9 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three indicators of underdevelopment (6 marks, two marks each: the indicator and its description).**

1. **Low income per person (GDP or GNP per capita).** Most people earn little, savings and investment are small, and a large part of the population lives in poverty, below the national poverty line.
2. **Poor health and high population indicators.** Life expectancy is low, birth rates, death rates and infant mortality are high, and many people suffer from malnutrition and diseases that can be prevented, because there are few doctors, hospitals and clean water supplies.
3. **Low level of education.** Adult literacy and school enrolment are low (especially for girls), and there are few skilled workers, which slows development.
4. **Other indicators that may be used:** a high share of the workers in agriculture and dependence on the export of raw materials, poor infrastructure (roads, electricity) and low energy use per person, high unemployment and under-employment, and a low score on the Human Development Index.

(Any three, each described.)

**(ii) Three techniques of climate-smart agriculture (3 marks, one mark each).**

1. **Growing drought-resistant, heat-tolerant and early-maturing crop varieties** (for example improved varieties of maize, cassava, sorghum).
2. **Soil and water conservation:** mulching and cover crops, conservation (reduced) tillage, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation such as drip irrigation.
3. **Agroforestry and crop diversification (crop rotation, intercropping):** trees on farms give shade, fix nitrogen and reduce soil erosion, and varied crops reduce the risk of a total loss.
4. Other techniques: using weather and early-warning information to choose the planting date, improved pasture and livestock management, and crop insurance.

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) (i) The following are farming aspects: rainfall, soil fertility, weeding, spraying, meat processing, milk, vegetables, tubers, electricity, tilling.
Rearrange them under the headings inputs, processes and output.
(ii) Outline **TWO** challenges of tropical agriculture.

(5+2=7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Farming aspects arranged as a system (5 marks, half a mark for each aspect).**

| Inputs | Processes | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Rainfall | Weeding | Milk |
| Soil fertility | Spraying | Vegetables |
| Electricity | Tilling | Tubers |
| | Meat processing | |

(Inputs are what is put into the farm system; processes are the operations carried out on the farm and on its products; output is what the farm produces. "Meat processing" is placed with the processes because it is an operation; a candidate who puts "meat" among the output because of the products it gives should be credited if the reason is clear.)

**(ii) Two challenges of tropical agriculture (2 marks, one mark each).**

1. **Pests, diseases and weeds.** The warm, humid climate favours insects, fungi and weeds that attack crops and animals (for example the tsetse fly for livestock), so losses are heavy and the cost of control is high.
2. **Unreliable rainfall and poor soils.** Droughts and floods destroy crops, and heavy rain leaches and erodes the soils, which lose their fertility quickly under continuous cultivation.

(Other challenges accepted: small farms and little capital or machinery, poor storage, roads and markets, price falls for export crops, and land-tenure problems.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Describe **TWO** importance of energy resources to an economy.

(4 marks)

Total (20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two importances (2 marks each: statement and description):

1. **Energy drives industry and production.** Electricity, oil and gas power factories, mines, farms and workshops, so output, employment and the national income increase; cheap and reliable energy attracts investors.
2. **Energy is needed for transport, services and for daily life.** Fuel moves goods and people, electricity serves hospitals, schools, offices, communications and homes, and so raises the standard of living.

(Other importances: an energy resource such as crude oil or hydroelectric power can be exported to earn foreign exchange and tax revenue; the energy sector creates jobs; and it supports the growth of infrastructure and towns.)
